narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Isolated Afternoon Showers & Thunderstorms lie ahead, reaching a high of 30°C (86°F) and dropping to a low of 20°C (68°F) tonight. Rain brings 2.5 mm (0.10 in) with a 76% chance between 16:00 – 20:00. Sky conditions move from early Partly cloudy to midday Mostly clear, then evening Partly cloudy. Winds are northerly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with peak gusts up to 33 km/h (18 kt). Thunder possible, peaking this evening. The UV peak index will reach 8.9. Air quality shows Kisumu Airport at AQI 54, 2 of 3 reporting. As of 07:37, reports through 06:30: no rain; no thunder; high so far 20°C (68°F); low so far 20°C (68°F); peak sustained 0 km/h (0 kt); sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS: temperatures and winds much the same through Friday, with showers possible Wednesday, dry Thursday and Friday, and thunderstorms likely each day. Wednesday remains Partly cloudy as four of four models wet with thunderstorms likely and high 30°C (86°F). Thursday stays Partly cloudy with two of four models wet and highs of 30–31°C (86–88°F). Friday, called dry at 30%, is Partly cloudy with one of four models wet and highs of 31–32°C (88–90°F). Saturday continues Partly cloudy with two of four models wet and highs of 30–32°C (86–90°F). Sunday turns Mostly cloudy with one of four models wet and highs of 30–33°C (86–91°F). Monday is Mostly cloudy with zero of three models wet and thunder possible. Tuesday, called rain at 59%, is Partly cloudy with one of two models wet.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values ahead indicate thunderstorm energy, reaching 1110 J/kg for GFS, 1920 J/kg for ECMWF, 1990 J/kg for ICON, 2670 J/kg for UKMO, and 1930 J/kg for Best Match, with energy peaking at 19:00. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No warning was issued by the met service.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Over Winam Gulf, winds are north-northeasterly overnight at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 10 km/h (6 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 18 km/h (10 kt), then into the evening at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 17 km/h (9 kt); peak gust 27 km/h (15 kt). Any thunderstorm carries the hazard of sudden gusts well above forecast winds.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is deepening over the next three days. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1013.5 and 1015.9 hPa; near-steady over three days (-1.3 hPa). Pressure overhead shows a trend of +0.4 hPa. Lower pressure lies toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others here yet across 73 checks, though GFS holds the best rain record, right 87% of the last 30 checks over 100 checks all time. Today's call for a 30°C (86°F) high sits slightly above GFS (29.4°C [84.9°F]), ECMWF (29°C [84°F]), ICON (29.1°C [84.4°F]), and Best Match (29.6°C [85.3°F]), matching UKMO (30°C [86°F]). The 20°C (68°F) low aligns between UKMO (18.1°C [64.6°F]) and ICON (22.8°C [73.0°F]). Rain volume of 2.5 mm (0.10 in) sits near ECMWF (2.7 mm [0.11 in]) and ICON (2.8 mm [0.11 in]), while peak gusts of 33 km/h (18 kt) sit near Best Match (33.1 km/h [18 kt]). GFS does not see this location's thunderstorms coming, sitting on the wrong side of its own strong rain record. ECMWF and Best Match under-forecast daytime highs and wind. No forecast bulletin came from the Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD). Data sufficiency is settled with 73 checks at Day+0, 37 checks at Day+3, and 94 checks at Day+7.
